sentences.text: Judgment
This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of .26,50,000/- for the death of Siddalingappa B.N. S/o Late Nijaguna, in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 25.02.2024, at about 6:15 a.m., Siddhalingappa was proceeding in a car bearing registration number KA- 05-NB-2525 along with his wife and son from Gubbi towards Srirangapatna to visit Nimishamba Temple.

When they were travelling on the NH-150(A) Highway road near Anchechittanahalli, Kasaba Hobli, Nagamangala taluk, Mandya District, the driver of a Bolero goods vehicle bearing registration number KA- 52-B-1828 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle") drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the car.
3. As a result of the accident, Siddhalingappa sustained grievous head injuries and died on the way to the hospital.
His wife, A.G. Sheela, also sustained multiple injuries and succumbed to the same.
Post- mortem examinations were conducted at Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Nagamangala, and thereafter, the deceased bodies were handed over to the petitioner.
4. The petitioner has stated that he spent a sum of Rs. 1,00,000 towards transportation of the dead bodies, funeral expenses, and obsequies.
It is further contended that the accident and resultant deaths occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged 60 years, and was engaged in running a Xerox shop, real estate business, and agricultural work, earning about Rs. 40,000 per month.

The petitioner, being the son of the deceased and financially dependent on his income, has therefore sought compensation of Rs. 26,50,000/- with interest, jointly and severally from Respondent No. 1 and Respondent No. 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
6. In response to the petition notice, Respondent No.2 appeared before this Tribunal through its counsel and filed a written statement.
Respondent No. 1 did not appear before the Court despite service of notice and was therefore placed ex parte.
7. Respondent No. 2, the Insurance Company, admitted the issuance of a valid insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
However, it contended that its liability, if any, is strictly subject to the terms and conditions of the said policy.
Respondent No. 2 denied all other averments made in the petition, including the allegations regarding the age, avocation, and income of the deceased, as well as the petitioner's dependency upon him.
It is further contended that the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant, and therefore prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that Sri.Siddalingappa B.N. S/o.Nijaguna died in a Road traffic accident occurred on 25-02-2024 at about 6.15 a.m., near Yashas B S vs Shivanna on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134218021/
2 Anchechittanahalli on NH-150(A) Road, Kasaba Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya district, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bolero goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-B-1828?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what amount?
3.
What order or award?
9. In support of the claim, Petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.11.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.
10. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record .

11. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly In the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1:-

Petitioner says that on 25.02.2024, at about 6:15 a.m., Siddhalingappa was proceeding in a car bearing registration number KA- 05-NB-2525 along with his wife and son from Gubbi towards Srirangapatna to visit Nimishamba Temple.

When they were travelling on the NH-150(A) Highway road near Anchechittanahalli, Kasaba Hobli, Nagamangala taluk, Mandya District, the driver of a the "offending vehicle" drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the car.
13. As a result of the accident, Siddhalingappa sustained grievous head injuries and died on the way to the hospital.
Petitioner says that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
He relied on the police records and it is requested to award compensation from the respondents.

14. Respondent No.2 (insurance) has denied the petition and asserted that the collision was a head-on collision and therefore contributory negligence is involved; and the driver of the car was also negligent.
15. Keeping in view of the rival contentions, the main question for consideration is whether there was any contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the car in causing the accident.

16. Petitioner examined himself as PW1 and relied on Ex.P1 to 3, EX P5 to P9, which include FIR,
Complaint, PM report, charge sheet, inquest report, spot mahazar with rough sketch, vehicle seizure mahazar, IMV report.

From Ex.P1 and P5 (FIR and charge sheet), it is evident that the case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle Yashas B S vs Shivanna on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134218021/
3 17.

entities.text: Yashas B S vs Shivanna on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The police, after investigation, have clearly opined that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
18. The spot mahazar and rough sketch show that the accident occurred on the NH-150A highway near Achittinahalli.
The position of vehicles and the nature of damage in the IMV report corroborate the version of the petitioner.
19. The respondent No.2-Insurance Company, though denied the negligence, has not produced any rebuttal evidence.
No eyewitness, mechanical report, or sketch was produced to establish that the accident occurred due to contributory negligence or collision impact from both sides.
During cross-examination of PW1, no material contradiction or admission was elicited to show that the driver of the car contributed to the occurrence of the accident.
20. It is well settled

that when the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle,
and no contrary evidence is placed, the tribunal can safely rely upon the same to hold negligence.
21.

The respondent no 2 has taken a plea that it was a case of "head-on collision," and therefore,
there was contributory negligence.
However, except for such suggestion, no cogent evidence is placed to prove the same.
Contributory negligence must be established by the party alleging it.
A mere assertion without proof cannot displace the charge sheet findings.
On careful scrutiny, it is evident that there is no material to indicate any negligence on the part of the deceased driver of the car.
22. The police investigation, contemporaneous records, and unshaken testimony of PW1 prove that the driver of the Bolero vehicle was driving in a rash and negligent manner, causing the accident.
Accordingly, it is held that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The plea of contributory negligence raised by Respondent No.2 is unsupported by evidence.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
23. ISSUE NO.2:- to establish the relationship with the deceased, the petitioner has produced the inquest report at EXP6 and his Voter ID card and deceased's Aadhaar card at Ex.P.10 and 11.
The records clearly indicate that deceased, Siddalingappa was the father of Petitioner.

Learned Counsel for Respondent No. 2 vehemently contended that the petitioner, being an earning member of the family, was not financially dependent on the deceased and hence cannot be treated as a dependent for the purpose of compensation.
However, merely being employed and earning some income does not, by itself, disentitle a claimant from being considered a dependent, especially in cases involving a parental relationship.

24. It is a settled principle of law that dependency is not to be determined solely on the basis of actual financial need but also on the existence of mutual care, support, and contribution within the family.
Even when the children are employed, if the deceased parent was earning more and contributing substantially to the family welfare, the element of dependency cannot be denied.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Various decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Courts have consistently held that where the deceased parent had a higher income and was providing financial or moral support, the children can still be treated as dependents for the purpose of assessing compensation.

Therefore,
without accepting the contention raised by Respondent No. 2, this Tribunal is of the considered view that the petitioner is a legal heir, and a dependent of the deceased.

26. On perusal of records, it is found that Petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card of deceased at Ex.P.11, which shows the year of birth of the deceased as 1960 and as such, age of the deceased is considered was 64 years at the time of accident and appropriate multiplier applicable is 7.
27.

It is stated that At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged 60 years, and was engaged in running a Xerox shop, real estate business, and agricultural work, earning about Rs. 40,000 per month.
The Petitioner, being the son of the deceased, financially dependent on his income and he was the bread earner of the family and contributing his entire earnings towards maintenance of the family.
28. To prove the income and avocation of the deceased, the Petitioner has not produced any documents.

In the absence of proof of income, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (KSLSA) for determining notional income in motor accident claims, since the accident occurred in the year 2024, the notional income is taken at Rs. 16,500/- per month.
29. As the deceased age was aged 64 years, no future prospects is added on the income of the deceased.

Since, petitioner is the sole dependent in the family and it is on record that his mother also died in the same accident, this tribunal holds that 50% of his income shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Then the income is .8,250 x 12=Rs.99,000/- .The loss of dependency would be .99,000 x 7 =.6,93,000/-.
30. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others., this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioner is entitled .44,000/- under the head of consortium as he has lost his father.

sentences.text: 31. Loss to estate:
It appears that the Petitioner has lost his father.
Hence, .20,000/- is awarded towards loss to estate.
32. Funeral Expenses:
Petitioner has claimed that they have spent .1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.

By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award .16,500/- for the funeral and other incidental expenses.
33.

In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioner under various headings is as follows :
Sl.No Nature of Compensation Amount 1. Loss of dependency Rs. 6,93,000/-

5 2. Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/-
to Petitioners 3. Loss to estate Rs. 20,000/-
4. Transportation of Rs. 16,500/-
dead body, Funeral & obsequies Expenses Total Rs. 7,73,500/-
34.
Liability:
The Petitioner has lead cogent evidence and has proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.7,73,500/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 2 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to him through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly over computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 8th day of October 2025).

(SHYLA S.M.) II Addl. Judge & ACJM, Member, MACT Court of Small Causes,
Bengaluru.
